evidence.mission_note: An S52 manual M Roadster is the preferred keeper configuration, but this is a keeper rather than the bridge car. At this price it competes with cash preservation in accelerated_bridge mode unless documentation proves it superior to cheaper comparable-mileage examples.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes, through photos, a clean-looking, apparently stock Cosmos Black 2000 M Roadster with a sound-appearing soft top and factory wheels and exhaust. The S52 engine, manual transmission, 36,900 miles, two owners and clean title are all seller statements with no VIN or report behind them. The seller names a specific service list from a Las Vegas BMW shop last year, but no invoice is shown. That service covered only fluids and minor bushings, not the cooling components or the rear structure that matter most on this model. Nothing in the listing or the photos examined here addresses the rear subframe or trunk floor, tire ages, leaks, or the interior, whose colour looks possibly lighter than the stated black in some photos. The asking price of $25,990 sits above the $18,841-$24,044 fair-value band. Close-mileage sold comps are around $19,500-$21,000, and the car has been listed about 47 weeks with cuts from $29,000. No issue is observed as wrong; the open items are documentation and the model's known weak points.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, the Las Vegas BMW shop invoices, tire date codes and trunk-floor and underside photos, and ask whether a PPI at a Las Vegas BMW independent is allowed before any deposit.
